- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect risk aversion or market panic.
- Model consistently overpredicts prices after sharp upward spikes in history; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or dampen momentum.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 5–10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently misses late-period rallies; add a “tail risk” buffer: if last 3 days show rising sentiment, increase final 3–5 days of forecast by 2–5%.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model tends to misalign with sentiment cycles; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
